data.title: Evaluating Diverse Large Language Models for Automatic and General Bug Reproduction

form.note: LIBRO is presented primarily as a proposed pipeline/technique for generating and postprocessing tests, rather than as a directly operated product. The paper notes that its implementation is public, but does not identify a user-facing product or interface.
form.evidence: we propose LIBRO, a pipeline that uses LLMs to first generate a number of BRT candidates

activity.note: LIBRO generates bug-reproducing test cases from bug reports, supporting test generation during software construction.
activity.evidence: By prompting LLMs to generate bug-reproducing tests

data.title: Improving Code Completion by Solving Data Inconsistencies in the Source Code with a Hierarchical Language Model

form.note: HLM is proposed and evaluated as a language model for code, rather than as a directly operated product or reusable library.
form.evidence: we propose a novel Hierarchical Language Model (HLM)

activity.note: The model predicts code tokens to support code completion.
activity.evidence: The proposed HLM takes the hierarchical structure of the code tree into consideration to predict code.

data.title: Automated Source Code Generation and Auto-Completion Using Deep Learning: Comparing and Discussing Current Language Model-Related Approaches

form.note: GPT-2 is presented as a pretrained transformer model that the authors fine-tune and evaluate, not as a directly operated product.
form.evidence: we used three standard pre-trained models as a basis: GPT-2, BERT, and RoBERTa

activity.note: The paper describes GPT-2 as predicting the next token to generate source code and evaluates its code-generation outputs.
activity.evidence: We chose to use GPT-2 since it is a causal transformer (unidirectional) that can predict the next token in a sequence. Therefore, it can generate source code based on the input
